journey.title: Open the filters drawer and apply a filter with the keyboard
journey.goal: Opening the drawer moves focus into it, so the user can tick a filter and show results without a pointer

functionalJourney.title: Apply a filter with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking Filters, ticking Waterproof and clicking Show results applies the filter

guards.title: Escape closes the drawer and returns focus to Filters
guards.goal: After opening the drawer with the pointer, Escape closes it and focus is back on the Filters button

plan.root_cause: The Drawer component inherits from DialogBase which uses native <dialog> showModal()/show() but does not override focus behavior. When opened via keyboard (Enter on trigger), the browser focuses the first focusable element in the drawer (the 'In stock' checkbox) instead of the close button. The test expects focus on the close button (#filters-close) for immediate keyboard dismissal.
plan.repair_strategy: Override _showElement in Drawer to explicitly focus the close button (identified by data-bs-dismiss="drawer") after calling the base implementation. This runs synchronously after showModal()/show() and overrides any browser auto-focus.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users opening the drawer via Enter on the trigger button will have focus land on the close button, enabling immediate Escape dismissal or Tab navigation to filter controls. Meets WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: Low risk: only adds a focus() call after existing show logic; no change to pointer/touch behavior.
Drawers without a close button (no data-bs-dismiss="drawer") are unaffected.
Does not interfere with Escape key regression guard which returns focus to trigger.
verification_requirements: Journey step 2 (Enter on #filters-open) must pass focus assertion on #filters-close.
Regression guard: Escape key closes drawer and returns focus to #filters-open.
Full keyboard journey (Tab, Space, Tab, Tab, Enter) must complete and update #applied to "in".
